title: Bug: FBX Rotations invert during animations

labels.name: Bug
labels.description: Global flag to mark a deviation from expected behaviour

labels.name: FBX
labels.description: Bugs related to the FBX format

labels.name: Animation
labels.description: Bugs related to the animation data

body:
When importing an FBX file with rotational animation keyframes, sometimes the resulting quaternion becomes inverted.

When one of my FBX files is imported into Blender, the animation data for one of the bones looks like this 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8890932/188494555-3e3c6ee4-1946-4c5a-9cd2-cbed92199ab2.png)

This inversion of rotations is causing issues when tweening between the afflicted keyframes.

I noticed that if I comment out [this line](https://github.com/assimp/assimp/blob/master/code/AssetLib/FBX/FBXConverter.cpp#L3264) (which will effectively disable the `for`), assimp will import the rotation keyframes correctly without inversions and the model will animate correctly. I don't fully understand why the loop needs to invert the transform data for each keyframe, but if it's necessary, then I expect the problem may be with either `aiQuaternion::GetMatrix` or `aiMatrix4x4::Decompose`.

**To reproduce**
[animationissue.zip](https://github.com/assimp/assimp/files/9491581/animationissue.zip)
1. Download this FBX file and load it with assimp's `Assimp::Importer importer; importer.ReadFile`. Evaluate the `upper_arm.R` bone animation data and it should correlate with the above output where rotations are inverted on frame 7 and uninverted on frame 23. 
2. Rebuild assimp with line FBXConverter.cpp:3264 `//mat.Decompose(s, r, t);` commented out and try loading the FBX again. Evaluate the `upper_arm.R` bone animation data and see that the rotation values no longer invert.

**Platform:**
 - OS: Windows 10
 - Compiler: g++.exe (Rev2, Built by MSYS2 project) 12.1.0
 - FBX version: 7400
 - Blender version: 3.1.0
